# IMPD-CS — Codebook v0.5.1

**IMPD-CS** is the cross-sectional component of the Integrated Migrant Panel Dataset (IMPD). It brings eight Dutch surveys of persons with a migration background, held between 2002 and 2020, together in one harmonized person-level file: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015 and SIM 2020. It covers 55,157 persons - the four largest origin groups (Turkish, Moroccan, Surinamese, Antillean/Aruban), refugee groups (Afghan, Iraqi, Iranian, former Yugoslav, Somali), Polish and Chinese migrants, and native Dutch reference samples - with 1,642 variables on demography, migration history, language, education, work, income, housing, health, social contacts, family, attitudes, religion and identity. Every variable has an English name grouped by theme, one coding across the surveys, and missing-value codes that say why a value is missing. The surveys are repeated cross-sections: the same persons are not followed from one survey to the next. The file is rebuilt in R or Stata from the survey files archived at DANS; the survey data themselves are not redistributed.

This codebook documents that file: what it contains, how each variable was built from the source surveys, and how to use it. It serves two kinds of reader. **Researchers who want to analyse the data** should begin with *Start here*, which walks through the steps of an analysis and links to the reference sections. **Readers who want to check or reproduce a variable** will find the rules in sections 2-3 and the evidence per variable in section 5. Section 1 describes the surveys, sections 2-3 the conventions and the questionnaires; section 4 is the index of all variables; section 5 holds one collapsible entry per variable. The shaded *more detail* blocks open on a click; they hold the full rules and survey-by-survey specifics, so the visible text stays short.

*Generated 2026-11-11 15:54 CET by `code/R/05_codebook.R` from the crosswalks in `crosswalks/` and the built data in `data/derived/`. **Build identity:** `7069c412771c` (sha256 of the crosswalks and the code, first 12 hex digits; also in `docs/run_log.md` and `docs/BUILD_ID`). Cite the build identity with the version: substantively different revisions can carry the same version number during development. How to cite: `CITATION.cff` in the repository root.*

## Start here
For researchers who want to run an analysis with the IMPD: the six steps below take you from the DANS deposits to a reported result, and each points to the section that holds the reference material. `docs/example_analysis.md` follows the same steps on one question asked in all eight surveys, in R (which also needs the `survey` package) and Stata (version 17 or later).
- **Rebuild the data.** The built file cannot be redistributed: rebuild it from the DANS deposits with `code/R/run_all.R` or `code/Stata/run_all.do` (instructions in the README).
- **Find measures.** Search the variable finder (HTML) or the [Variable index](#index) (section 4) and check that the measure exists in your surveys; `docs/codebook_variables.csv` is the same index as a table.
- **Inspect the measures.** Open their [Variable descriptions](#descriptions) (section 5): the exact question per survey, how the value was obtained, the categories and recodes, who was eligible, and how comparable the surveys are. A comparability class is a reading aid, not a certification.
- **Define your study population.** Section 1 ([What this dataset is](#what)) describes who was sampled in each survey; each measure's eligibility statement says who was asked. `svy_routing_mig`, `dem_eth`, `dem_gen` and `svy_resptype` identify the groups.
- **Check the joint sample.** `impd_sample` (R: `code/R/impd_tools.R`; Stata: `code/Stata/impd_tools.do`) shows per survey how many complete cases remain and why records drop out, and stops when a survey would disappear from the model unnoticed; `impd_universe()` (R only) prints the eligibility statements of a set of variables.
- **Run and report the analysis.** State the population, the [weighting and pooling choice](#weights) and the final sample by survey.

## 1. What this dataset is {#what}
IMPD-CS covers the eight surveys below, in the versions archived at DANS. Two are **household samples** of migrant households in a set of municipalities, conducted by ISEO (SPVA 2002 and SPVN 2003, the latter for refugee groups); six are **person samples** drawn by CBS from the population register and conducted for SCP (LAS 2004/05 to SIM 2020), each with a native Dutch reference sample. This section lists the surveys, says what a row of the file is, and who was eligible in each survey and how it is weighted. The surveys covered:

### What a row is {#rows}

Each row is a person (55,157 in total). In the two **household samples** (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003) a row is a member listed in the household roster: the head of household (main questionnaire), another member aged 12+ (mini questionnaire), or a roster-only member who was not interviewed. In the six **person samples** (LAS 2004/05 to SIM 2020) a row is an individually sampled respondent; these surveys also include a **native Dutch reference sample** (`dem_eth` = 90), which skips the items asked only of persons with a migration background (`.c`). `svy_resptype` tells the record types apart:

| Survey | Head of household - main questionnaire | Household member - roster only, not interviewed | Individually sampled respondent (person sample) | Other household member - mini questionnaire | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPVA2002 | 4199 | 5183 | 0 | 4122 | 13504 |
| SPVN2003 | 3547 | 3525 | 0 | 2047 | 9119 |
| LAS2004 | 0 | 0 | 4096 | 0 | 4096 |
| SIM2006 | 0 | 0 | 5250 | 0 | 5250 |
| SING2009 | 0 | 0 | 6911 | 0 | 6911 |
| SIM2011 | 0 | 0 | 4125 | 0 | 4125 |
| SIM2015 | 0 | 0 | 6829 | 0 | 6829 |
| SIM2020 | 0 | 0 | 5323 | 0 | 5323 |

<details class='more'><summary>Identifiers and household variables</summary>

In the household samples (SPVA/SPVN) a row is a **household member listed in the survey roster**; `svy_resptype` distinguishes heads of household (main questionnaire), other members aged 12+ (mini questionnaire) and roster-only members (no interview; demographic information reported by the head), and household-level variables (`hh_*`) are taken from the head's record and merged onto every member. In the person samples (LAS, SIM, SING) every row is an **individually sampled respondent** (`svy_resptype` = 4) drawn from the population register; there is no household identifier (`id_hh` = `.e`) and the `hh_*` variables describe the respondent's own household (self-reported or from the registry, suffix `_reg`). These files include the **native Dutch reference samples** (`dem_eth` = 90, `dem_gen` = 0); items asked only to persons with a migration background are `.c` for them. `svy_id` numbers the surveys chronologically (SPVA 2002 = 5 ... SIM 2020 = 12; the numbering leaves room for surveys added later); `id_person` = `svy_key` x 10^11 + the record number of the deposit, where `svy_key` is the fieldwork year (immutable, so identifiers do not change when a survey is added); SIM 2006 and SING 2009 ship no respondent number and the row number of the deposited file is used. In the household samples `id_prtnr` links the head of household and the co-resident partner to each other's record (section 2).

</details>


### Eligibility and weights {#weights}

IMPD-CS is a set of **repeated cross-sections, not a panel**: the same person is not followed across surveys, and `id_person` identifies a record within one survey only (the 'panel' in the project name refers to the registry-linked component, IMPD-P, built separately on the CBS microdata). Each survey has its own target population and its own weight, `svy_wgt`, which reproduces that population. The weights are therefore not comparable across surveys and are not a pooled population weight: when you pool surveys, decide how the waves contribute and say so (wave-specific estimates, or the wave as an explicit stratum, are often the clearer choice), and account for the clustering of household members in SPVA/SPVN (`id_hh`). Every analysis should state which surveys contribute, who was eligible in each, and which weight it uses.

<details class='more'><summary>Eligible sample and weights per survey</summary>

| Survey | Eligible sample / target population | Weights |
|---|---|---|
| SPVA 2002 | Households of Turkish, Moroccan, Surinamese and Antillean/Aruban origin in 13 municipalities (ISEO; the native comparison sample is not in the DANS deposit). Rows: all roster members; interviewed persons = heads (main questionnaire) and members aged 12+ (mini); children and non-interviewed members are roster-only records with head-reported demography. | svy_wgt: ISEO design/post-stratification weight of the household (merged onto every member). Not a population weight across surveys; observations are clustered within households (id_hh). |
| SPVN 2003 | Households of Afghan, Iraqi, Iranian, former-Yugoslav and Somali origin in 12 municipalities (ISEO). Same row structure as SPVA 2002. | svy_wgt: ISEO household weight; cluster on id_hh. |
| LAS 2004/05 | Persons aged 15-64 of Turkish, Moroccan, Surinamese, Antillean/Aruban and native Dutch origin in the 50 largest municipalities (GBA sample, CBS); 228 persons belong to an oversample of working men and women (svy_oversample). | svy_wgt (weegtot): Veldkamp/SCP weight to the population of the 50 largest municipalities; svy_wgt_grp (weegherk): weight within origin group (mean 1 per group); svy_wgt_raise (ophtot): raising factor to population totals. Diary analyses: tim_wgt / tim_wgt_corr. |
| SIM 2006 | Persons aged 15+ of Turkish, Moroccan, Surinamese, Antillean/Aruban and native Dutch origin, nationwide GBA sample (CBS). | svy_wgt (weegtot): CBS weight to the national population of the five groups; svy_wgt_grp (weegherk): within origin group; svy_wgt_raise (ophtot): raising factor. |
| SING 2009 | Persons aged 15+ of Afghan, Iraqi, Iranian, Somali, Chinese, Polish (short-stay, registered < 5 years) and native Dutch origin, nationwide two-stage GBA sample (CBS); partial release (see section 3). | svy_wgt = svy_wgt_grp (weegherk): within-origin-group weight, the only general weight in the deposit; svy_wgt_pool: separate weight for the short-stay Polish sample. No weight to a pooled national population is supplied. |
| SIM 2011 | Persons aged 15+ of Turkish, Moroccan, Surinamese, Antillean/Aruban and native Dutch origin, nationwide GBA sample stratified by municipality size (CBS); main CAPI study only. | svy_wgt (weegtot): CBS weight to the national population (origin x sex, household size/marital status, municipality stratum, generation, age); svy_wgt_grp (weegherk): within origin group; svy_wgt_raise (ophtot): raising factor. |
| SIM 2015 | Persons aged 15+ of Turkish, Moroccan, Surinamese, Antillean/Aruban, Somali, Polish (first generation registered 2004+) and native Dutch origin, nationwide BRP sample (CBS). | svy_wgt (eindgewicht): CBS calibration weight scaled to the population; svy_wgt_alt: alternative weighting model; svy_wgt_start: inverse selection probability. |
| SIM 2020 | Persons aged 15+ of Turkish, Moroccan, Surinamese, Caribbean-Dutch, Somali, Polish (first generation registered 2004+), Iranian and native Dutch origin, nationwide BRP sample (CBS); split-half questionnaire (svy_split). | svy_wgt (eindgewicht): CBS calibration weight scaled to the population. |

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>Pooling, rescaling and design-based variances</summary>


The survey weights are survey-specific (different target populations, age ranges, designs and calibration models) and are not comparable across surveys: `svy_wgt` reproduces each survey's own target population and is not a pooled population weight. Within one survey the weight can be used as supplied. When surveys are pooled, the analyst decides how the waves contribute to the intended estimate and says so: rescaling the weights within survey (to equal sums, or to the sample sizes) only sets the relative contribution of the waves and does not define a common pooled population, because the target populations differ (section 1); wave-specific estimates, or the wave as an explicit stratum, are often the clearer choice. Account for the household clustering of SPVA/SPVN (`id_hh`) and the stratified designs of the person samples; no replicate or stratum variables are deposited, so design-based variances beyond the clustering are not available. The worked example in `docs/example_analysis.md` shows one such choice in full.

</details>


## 2. Conventions {#conventions}
How variables are named and coded, what the missing-value codes mean, and what each variable entry in section 5 tells you. Subsections 2.1-2.3 are what most users need; 2.4-2.5 are reference.

### 2.1 Variable names {#names}
Names are `theme_concept` in English, built as `stem_[sub_]item[_suffix]`: the stem gives the theme (`dem_` demography, `lab_` labour market, `att_` attitudes ...), and items of a battery that share one question are numbered in questionnaire order (`att_gr01`, `lab_srch03`). The most frequent suffixes are `_cat` (harmonized classes) and `_det` (survey-specific detail), `_lvl3` (three education levels), `_15` (constant 2015 euro), `_reg` (registry-based) and `_txt` (open text). Every variable's label spells its name out.

<details class='more'><summary>Naming rules and all suffixes</summary>

Names are `stem_[sub_]item[_suffix]`, kept short with recurring abbreviations; items of a battery sharing one question stem are numbered in questionnaire order (e.g. `att_gr01`, `lab_srch03`) and the battery prefix says what the scale is. Suffixes: `_cat` harmonized classes, `_det` survey-specific detail, `_cat5` five classes incl. none, `_lvl3` three education levels (SCP laag/middel/hoog), `_15` constant 2015 euro, `_yr`/`_mo` year/month, `_yrs` duration in years, `_n` count, `_txt` open text, `_reg` registry-based (CBS) variable, `_cbs` CBS three-class migration background, a trailing number of points (`_4`, `_10`) the scale length where the same construct was asked on different scales.

The abbreviations used inside names are listed in `crosswalks/name_glossary.csv` (kind 'abbreviation'); every variable's label spells its name out.

</details>

### 2.2 Codes and types {#codes}
Where the surveys use incompatible detailed codings of the same concept, a variable ending in `_cat` holds the harmonized classes and one ending in `_det` keeps the survey-specific detail with the survey named in the value label (e.g. `edu_abr_hi_cat` / `edu_abr_hi_det`). Binary items are coded 1 = yes, 0 = no; multiple-response items 1 = mentioned, 0 = not mentioned; agreement items keep 1 = strongly agree … 5 = strongly disagree.
Variable types: `cat` = coded categories with a value set (frequencies shown), `num` = quantity (summary statistics shown), `year` = calendar year, `str` = text, `id` = identifier: a dimensionless number that singles out a respondent, household or survey record; the codebook reports only coverage and uniqueness for identifiers, never descriptives.

### 2.3 Missing values {#missing}
Missing values carry a reason, as Stata extended missing values (R: `haven::tagged_na`) that survive the round trip between the `.dta` and `.rds` files. The distinction that matters most in analysis is between **`.c`** (the person was routed past the question) and **`.e`** (the survey, or this person's questionnaire, did not contain it):

| Code | Meaning | In short |
|---|---|---|
| .a | Don't know | The respondent did not know. |
| .b | Refusal | The respondent refused or gave no answer. |
| .c | Not applicable | The question did not apply: the person was routed past it (including the native reference sample for items asked only of persons with a migration background, and the other half of the SIM 2020 split-half questionnaire). |
| .d | No information | No information for another or unknown reason ('geen informatie', 'onbekend', unexplained empty cells). |
| .e | Not collected (survey/questionnaire) | The variable is not in this survey, or the item was not in this person's questionnaire (e.g. roster-only members, or a heads-only item for other household members). |

Plain system-missing (`.`) occurs only in SPVA/SPVN, whose files do not separate 'routed out' from 'not applicable'.

<details class='more'><summary>Which source codes map to which missing tag, per survey</summary>

The full assignment rules, survey by survey:

| Code | Meaning | Assigned when |
|---|---|---|
| .a | Don't know | Source code labelled 'weet niet' / declared don't-know code (SPVN: -3, 0 in year/month items, 7, 97/997/9997; LAS 2004/05: -3, -4, 999 'weet niet, geen informatie'; SIM 2006: -3; SING 2009: labelled 'weet niet'; SIM 2011: -3; SIM 2015: -3; SIM 2020: -3, -6) |
| .b | Refusal | Refusal / no answer: SPVN -2; LAS -2 and 'wil niet zeggen'; SIM 2006 -2; SING 'geen antwoord' / 'wil niet zeggen'; SIM 2011 -2; SIM 2015 -1 and 98 'wil niet zeggen'; SIM 2020 -2 'wil niet antwoorden' and -4 'geen antwoord' |
| .c | Not applicable | Not applicable: routed past the question - LAS -5/-7/-9 and 'niet gesteld'; SIM 2006 -5, -7 'niet in vragenlijst', -9; SING 'niet van toepassing'; SIM 2011 -5, -9 'nvt: autochtoon' and -1 (undocumented, used where a question was not asked); SIM 2015 -2 'blanc' and -5; SIM 2020 -5 'nvt binnen vragenlijst'; SIM constructed/coarsened variables where the routing question says so (derive kl9_route); native reference sample for migrant-only items; SPVA/SPVN: explicit 'not applicable' codes only. In LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006 and SING 2009 every remaining system-missing value is .c (the files leave routed-out cells empty) |
| .d | No information | No information: source code labelled 'geen informatie'/'missing'/'onbekend', SPVN -4, SIM 2006 -4/-8, SIM 2011 -4, SPSS user-missing codes declared in the SPVA file (9/99/999/9999), SIM 2020 code 9 'Anders/Refusal/Don't know' of the coarsened (_kl) variables, SIM 2015 -4/-6 in constructed variables, and any remaining system-missing value in the SIM 2011, 2015 and 2020 files |
| .e | Not collected (survey/questionnaire) | Variable not in this survey, or item not in this respondent's questionnaire: in SPVA/SPVN a heads-file item for other members, any item for roster-only members, and the items of `crosswalks/asked_to.csv` that the persons file holds for both types but only one type was asked (main-questionnaire blocks L-M of SPVA 2002 for other members; mini-questionnaire items for heads). The split-half block of the other group in SIM 2020 is .c, not .e |

Plain system-missing (`.`) occurs only in SPVA/SPVN and means the item was routed out or not applicable in the source (those files do not allow the two to be separated); in the person-sample surveys every missing value is tagged, with the survey-specific tag for untagged empty cells recorded in `crosswalks/surveys.csv` (`sysmis_tag`: .c for LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006 and SING 2009, whose files only leave routed-out cells empty; .d for SIM 2011-2020, where empty cells also arise from item non-response in constructed variables). Rules: `crosswalks/missing_rules.csv` (per survey: code rules, label rules, declared-code rules); the declared SPSS user-missing codes per variable: `crosswalks/source_missing.csv`; the routing rules for SIM constructed variables: `code/R/03_derive.R` (kl9_route).

</details>


### 2.4 What a variable entry tells you {#entries}
Every entry in section 5 states whom the value describes (**Subject**: self, partner, child, household ...), who supplied it in each survey (**Reported by**: the respondent, the head of household, the interviewer, the registry ...), whether each survey collected or derived it (**Availability**), and a **Comparability** class over the surveys that carry it (exact, coarse or approximate match, mixed provenance, construct-defined, derived, wave-specific). The class is a reading aid, not a certification: it says whether the texts and codes agree, not whether mode, context or population do. A wording table then shows, survey by survey, the question and how it was asked (section 3.1).

<details class='more'><summary>Subject, reporter, availability and comparability classes in full</summary>

Every variable entry states whom the value describes (`Subject`: self, partner, child, selected child, parent, household, interview, identifier), who supplied it per survey (`Reported by`: the respondent; the head of household for roster members or household items; the partner's own record through the roster link `id_prtnr` in SPVA/SPVN; the interviewer; the sample frame or registry; the data producer for constructed variables), how each survey contributes (`Availability`: collected, derived, derived from the roster link, not collected) and a comparability class over the surveys that carry it (`Comparability`: exact match = same question and answer options in every respondent-facing source, or the same interviewer instruction and recording categories where the value is interviewer-acquired; coarse match = harmonized classes of finer survey-specific codings; approximate match = same construct with different wording or scales, read the wording table; mixed provenance = the information is obtained differently across surveys - a respondent report in some, an interviewer recording, a registry field or a constructed variable in others - so the measurements are not equivalent by wording; construct-defined = constructed/registry in every survey; derived; wave-specific; administrative). How each source was obtained is stated per source in the wording table (`How obtained`: respondent report, proxy report about a partner/child/parent, interviewer recording without asking, interviewer assessment, interviewer observation, interview administration, registry/sample data, derived/coded; `crosswalks/wording.csv` columns `acquisition`, `respondent_facing`, `supplied_by`, `describes`; declared cases in `crosswalks/acquisition_overrides.csv`). The class is seeded mechanically from the wording components and the variable's construction (`status` auto) and can be overridden by a reviewer in `crosswalks/comparability_review.csv` (`status` reviewed); the whole inventory is `docs/comparability.csv`. A class is a reading aid, not a certification: 'exact match' says the texts and codes agree, not that mode, context or population do.

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>Partner variables in the household samples (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)</summary>

SPVA 2002 and SPVN 2003 interview the head of household and list the partner as a record of her/his own; `id_prtnr` links the two (the other head/partner member of the roster, `dem_poshh` 0/1; `.c` = no co-resident partner record, `.d` = other household members, whose partner is not identifiable). Two kinds of variable are derived from it. (a) The partner characteristics that the person samples ask as proxy questions (`dem_prtnr_sex`, `dem_prtnr_age*`, `dem_prtnr_brthcntry`, `dem_prtnr_eth`, `dem_prtnr_gen`, `edu_prtnr_lvl3`, `dem_prtnr_emp`, `dem_prtnr_hrs`, `mig_yr_arr_prtnr`, `mig_reason_prtnr`) are copied from the linked partner's own record where the survey did not ask them, so their acquisition and reporter are those of the base field (`dem_prtnr_sex` carries the interviewer's recording of the partner's sex, `edu_prtnr_lvl3` the coded diploma): `.c` = no co-resident partner; `.d` = other household members, and partners listed in the roster but not interviewed where the base item needs an interview - roster demography (sex, age, country of birth) is available for them, and the base field's own missing tags are kept. (b) The relationship indicators `dem_has_prtnr` and `dem_prtnr_cores` are computed from the link and the living-apart-together question, including for persons without a partner record: co-resident link -> 1/1, LAT partner without a link -> 1/0, identifiable head/partner without link or LAT partner -> 0/`.c`, other members -> `.d`. Each variable's wording table states its own rule. Children are not linked (the person samples describe one selected child or children in general; roster children are rows of their own, summarised by `hh_nchd*`).

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>Country codes, municipalities, occupations, industries and euro amounts</summary>

**Country codes** (`dem_brthcntry*`, `dem_prtnr_brthcntry`, `mig_tr_cntry*`) follow the Dutch GBA/BRP *Landentabel* (Tabel 34, RVIG; `External/Country codes/landentabel34.csv`), with project codes 9901 other Africa, 9902 other Asia, 9903 other Europe, 9998 unidentifiable name, 9999 other country; 7011 is used as an aggregate for the (former) Netherlands Antilles, Aruba and the Caribbean Netherlands. In SIM the public files contain no country of birth: `dem_brthcntry` is derived from origin group x generation under the CBS definition (first generation = born in the origin country, second generation = born in the Netherlands). **Municipalities** carry the CBS gemeentecode of the 2006 list (SPVA/SPVN only; SIM gives urbanisation of the municipality, `geo_urb_reg`). **Occupations** are SBC-92 codes and **industries** SBI-93 codes as coded by ISEO; SIM 2015 industry is SBI 2008 (`lab_ind_sbi08`). **Euro amounts** are nominal as collected (SPVA/SPVN asked in euro); `*_15` versions are deflated with the CBS CPI (70936ENG, 2015 = 100; factors 2002: 1.2386, 2003: 1.2131, 2005: 1.1787 for the SIM 2006 transfer amounts that refer to calendar year 2005, 2009: 1.1062). SIM incomes are registry income bands (`inc_*_reg`, nominal euro of the income year) or self-reported bands and are not deflated.

</details>


### 2.5 Source files, access and reproducibility {#files}
Alongside the harmonized file, each survey has a **companion source file** with every original variable (prefix `src_`, Dutch labels, original codes), keyed by `id_person`, so any harmonization step can be checked or redone. The harmonized file itself **cannot be redistributed**, because six of the eight deposits are DANS *request permission* files: the public deliverable is the code, the crosswalks and this codebook, from which anyone with access to the deposits rebuilds the data. Every rule lives in the CSV crosswalks and is executed identically by the R and Stata pipelines.

<details class='more'><summary>Companion source files and weights</summary>

**Companion source files** `impd_cs_v0_5_1_source_<survey>.dta/.rds` contain every original variable of each survey (prefix `src_`, Dutch labels, original codes) keyed by `id_person`, so any harmonization step can be audited or redone. In the household surveys a field that occurs in more than one deposit file (heads, interviewed persons, roster) is kept once, with the value of the most detailed file (heads > persons > roster); where the files disagree - in SPVN 2003, 37 roster-age cells of 17 persons - the companion holds the chosen value only, and the per-file frames in `data/interim/` are the place to study the disagreement. **Weights** (`svy_wgt`) are the survey-specific weights supplied with the files: ISEO/SCP design weights for SPVA/SPVN, CBS calibration weights scaled to the population for SIM (SIM 2015 also ships an alternative model, `svy_wgt_alt`); they are not comparable across surveys (section 1, weights).

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>Access, redistribution and the SING 2009 partial release</summary>

**Access and redistribution.** SPVA 2002 and SPVN 2003 are open-access DANS deposits; LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020 are DANS *request permission* deposits (SCP/CBS files under the DANS licence); a harmonized file that contains their content therefore cannot be redistributed openly. The public deliverable of the IMPD is the code, the crosswalks and this codebook: anyone with access to the 8 DANS deposits rebuilds the data file with `code/R/run_all.R` or `code/Stata/run_all.do`. SING 2009 is a partial release: the deposit contains only the questions listed in its READ ME, with years and durations coarsened into classes (hence the `_cat` variants that exist for SING only) and with statistical protection applied to some variables - real values replaced by 'don't know' / 'not applicable' / 'other' codes for a few respondents (sex, marital status, origin group, generation, year of marriage), household size and number of children top-coded at 6 - so that the resulting missing and 'unknown' values are protection, not non-response (section 3, release).

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>Reproducibility and the value-map review</summary>

**Reproducibility.** `code/R/run_all.R` (R) and `code/Stata/run_all.do` (Stata) rebuild everything from the DANS zip files in `Surveys/` using only the CSV crosswalks; `code/crosswalk_builder/` documents how the crosswalks themselves were authored. Every value-map row can be read with its source label against the target label in `docs/value_map_review.csv`; the rows that the automatic label check cannot read by itself (two-valued targets with a non-yes/no source label, rows copied across surveys whose labels differ, range labels) carry a signed reading in `crosswalks/label_approvals.csv`, bound to the value that was read, and the builder refuses a crosswalk set with an unsigned or changed row (`code/tools/value_map_review.py`; check 16). Decisions and known limitations are listed in `docs/decisions.md`; the run log in `docs/run_log.md`.

</details>


## 3. Survey designs, questionnaires and randomisation {#designs}
Harmonization aligns codes, not questions: the same concept was asked in different words, modes and orders across the eight surveys. This section explains how to read the **wording tables** that document this per variable in section 5 (3.1), and describes the **design of each survey** - interview mode, question order and randomisation, routing, languages and what the deposit releases (3.2).

### 3.1 Reading the wording tables {#wording}
Each variable entry in section 5 has a wording table with one column per survey. It gives the source variable, **how the value was obtained** (respondent report, proxy report about a partner or child, interviewer recording, registry or derived), the **question or statement as shown or read to the respondent**, the answer options, who was eligible, and the **routing translated into harmonized variables** (e.g. `svy_routing_mig` in {1}), with a check of whether the data agree. Above the table, a `Wording` line compares the surveys component by component; 'differs' is a prompt to read the table, not a verdict that the measures are incomparable. The texts are parsed from the questionnaires in the DANS deposits.

<details class='more'><summary>What the rows of the wording table contain</summary>

Harmonization aligns codes, not questions: the per-variable **wording tables** in section 5 show, survey by survey, the source variable and its questionnaire reference, **how the value was obtained** (`How obtained`: respondent report; proxy report about a partner, child or parent; interviewer recording without asking; interviewer assessment; interviewer observation; interview administration; registry/sample data; derived/coded), who supplied the information and whom it describes, the introduction or lead-in, the **question or statement shown or read to the respondent** (the battery statement once, in its own row; for the formats that print the statement inside the question, the lead-in moves to the introduction row), the interviewer recording or assessment instruction (exact text, kept apart from the prompt), the response or recording categories, the response format, the source definition or derivation for registry and constructed sources, the value labels in the data file (the data label is printed as a gloss next to the source variable), the eligible records, the **routing in terms of harmonized variables** (the gate variable and the values under which the item was asked, with the empirical verdict; 'none printed' when the questionnaire prints no eligibility condition for the item; 'printed condition not mapped' when it prints one that no rule translates), and any split-half or randomisation note. The 'Response format' row holds numeric bounds, widgets and units, which are not spoken text. Curated notes flag changes that matter for comparability (e.g. 'allochtoon' -> 'persoon met een migratieachtergrond', changed answer scales).

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>Respondent-facing and interviewer-acquired sources</summary>

A source is respondent-facing only when a prompt was shown or read to the respondent: an item the interviewer records silently ('noteer stilzwijgend geslacht'), rates ('stel vast hoe goed de respondent Nederlands spreekt'), observes or completes about the interview, a [SAMPLE DATA] field and a coded variable are not, and their prompt row says so explicitly ('Not applicable - ...'; 'Question text not located' is a different state). Those classifications are phrase-based and narrow - an 'ENQ.:' note attached to a real question leaves the question respondent-facing - with declared cases in `crosswalks/acquisition_overrides.csv` and assertions in the builder and the renderer (no 'do not ask' / 'record silently' / assessment / sample-data item is respondent-facing; recording categories survive instruction-only blocks; no procedure or English description is printed as a prompt; no statement is printed twice).

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>How routing conditions are translated and checked against the data</summary>

The 'Routing (harmonized variables)' row translates the printed routing condition into the harmonized variable that carries the same information and the values under which the question was asked - by hand-written rules for the recurring conditions (`crosswalks/routing_rules.csv`: e.g. 'INDIEN ALLOCHTOON' -> `svy_routing_mig` in {1}, 'INDIEN MOSLIM' -> `rel_den_cat` in {2}) and automatically for conditions that reference a question number ('IF [ Q1450 , 1 ]', 'ASK ONLY IF not Q235=1', 'INDIEN JA:' after the preceding question): the referenced question is looked up in the same questionnaire, its codes are translated with the value map (negations taken over the observed source codes, don't-know/refusal codes as missing-tag gates, numeric comparisons kept), and the gate is stated on the harmonized variable; conditions that combine alternatives or compare two questions are not translated and say so; each gate is then verified against the data (per source variable, `docs/routing_check.csv`): 'holds in the data' means no value lies outside the gate, 'holds with exceptions' gives the count of values outside it (the data as delivered; e.g. a few second-generation respondents with a year of arrival), and a printed condition that the data contradict (a grid condition governing a sibling item, a constructed variable filled for everyone) is listed as 'not applied' with the reason (`crosswalks/routing_exceptions.csv`). A gate with more than 10% of its values outside fails the build (check 11), so users can reproduce the routing with variables of the harmonized file. The printed condition itself is not a table row: it is quoted inside the routing cell only when no rule translates it, and the full text (with skip instructions such as '2 -> naar 1519', text fills and display settings) stays as provenance in `crosswalks/wording.csv`, columns `routing`, `routing_skip`, `routing_script`. The same routing summary is given per variable above the table ('Routing (harmonized variables)'), survey by survey.

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>How the Wording line compares the surveys</summary>

The `Wording` line compares the surveys that carry the item **by acquisition family and component**: over the respondent-facing sources the question or battery statement (compared at the same level in every format), the introduction/lead-in, the answer options, the instructions and the routing; over the interviewer-acquired sources the instruction and the recording categories ('Procedure/scale'); registry and constructed sources are named and compared through their definitions, not their wording; and when the families differ between surveys the line says that the measurements are not equivalent by wording. Each component is reported as identical, identical except group fill, differs (naming the surveys that share each version), none printed, or printed in one survey only. Case, punctuation and group fills (<groep>, <?>, '*? HERKOMST') are ignored; other parentheticals are kept, so a changed qualifier shows as a difference. 'differs' is a prompt to read the table: it signals that the texts are not the same, not that the measurement is incomparable, and 'identical' for the question does not certify equivalence when options, introduction or administration differ.

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>Where the question texts come from, and caveats per survey</summary>

The texts are parsed from the questionnaire PDFs in the DANS deposits (`crosswalks/questionnaire_items.csv`; the full printed block of every item is kept as provenance in `crosswalks/wording.csv`, column `block_text`). Caveats: the SPVA 2002 texts are those of the Turkish-group main questionnaire deposited with the data (the Moroccan, Surinamese, Antillean and native versions differ only in the group fills, e.g. 'Turken' / 'Turkse'), and the SPVN 2003 texts those of the main questionnaire; the mini questionnaire for household members repeats the items marked '+G' in those codebooks. SIM 2015 texts are the CAWI version (the parallel CAPI question id is given). The LAS 2004/05 questionnaire is appendix 1a of the fieldwork report deposited with the data (`Bijlage 3 Veldwerkverslag`); the SIM 2011 questionnaire is the hardcopy of the CAPI script (appendix g). SIM 2006 and SING 2009 are deposited as Veldkamp CAPI script printouts that print no variable names: their items are linked to the data through the question number that the data labels carry ('Vraag 965: ...'), and for multiple-response questions through the option order (match 'qnum' / 'manual' in `crosswalks/wording.csv`). Coded and constructed variables (e.g. the SPVA/SPVN 'MAXDIP', 'BERBEV', 'INKOMEN2' family) and registry variables have no question text; where the codebook prints such a variable name after a question block, the table says so. The parse of the two-column SPVA 2002 codebook is less clean than that of the other three: grid scales appear as 'grid scale (labels in the data file)', and the printed answer codes of multi-line options were re-aligned by order. Fills such as <GROEP>, <land van herkomst> or <?> stand for text inserted per origin group by the survey software. Everything in the tables is data: `crosswalks/wording.csv`, `crosswalks/wording_notes.csv`, `crosswalks/universes.csv`, `crosswalks/questionnaire_constructed.csv`.

</details>


### 3.2 Survey designs {#surveydesign}
All eight surveys were face-to-face interviews except SIM 2015 (web first, then face-to-face) and SIM 2020 (mostly web). Randomisation matters in three surveys: SING 2009 asked one item to a random half, SIM 2015 randomised the item order within some batteries, and SIM 2020 used a **split-half questionnaire** (`svy_split`: 2,664 respondents in half A, 2,657 in half B; items of the other half are `.c`) as well as randomised item order. Open a survey for its design features (`crosswalks/questionnaire_design.csv`).

<details class='more'><summary>SPVA 2002 - Face-to-face (PAPI), household sample</summary>

- *mode*: Face-to-face interviews at home (paper questionnaires); main questionnaire for the head of household, mini questionnaire for other members aged 12+, cultural-integration module for one child aged 15+. Turkish/Arabic translated questionnaires available for the Turkish and Moroccan groups.
- *order*: Fixed question order (paper); no randomisation. Question blocks: general/household/migration, education, labour, income, health, language, group, social contacts, cultural integration, religion, imaging, family relations.
- *versions*: One questionnaire version per group; differences limited to the answer categories for mother tongue and ethnic subgroup.

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>SPVN 2003 - Face-to-face (CAPI), household sample</summary>

- *mode*: Face-to-face (CAPI) interviews; main questionnaire (15 blocks) for heads, mini questionnaire for members aged 12+, separate health and cultural-integration blocks for the partner and one child aged 15+; Dutch, English or French.
- *order*: Fixed question order; no randomisation.

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>LAS 2004/05 - Face-to-face (CAPI)</summary>

- *mode*: Face-to-face CAPI interviews (Veldkamp with TNS NIPO interviewers) with persons aged 15-64 sampled by CBS from the GBA of the 50 largest municipalities (Turks, Moroccans, Surinamese, Antilleans/Arubans, native Dutch); only the sampled person was interviewed. Fieldwork October 2004 - May 2005; corrected response 45% (Turks 47%, Moroccans 44%, Surinamese 38%, Antilleans 47%, natives 50%). An extra sample of working mothers with children under 12 was drawn in March 2005 in nine municipalities and the working partners of male Turkish, Moroccan and Antillean respondents with young children were asked a supplementary interview (47 cases; items marked '+ P' in the questionnaire, of which only dem_prtnr_flex survives as a separate variable); svy_oversample flags the resulting oversample of working men and women (228 cases).
- *order*: Fixed block order A-X; no rotation or randomisation reported. Questions on the murder of Theo van Gogh were added about two weeks into the fieldwork (universe: respondents interviewed after that point).
- *routing*: One programmed questionnaire with group routing (INDIEN ALLOCHTOON / AUTOCHTOON / TURK, MAROKKAAN / MOSLIM / NIET IN NEDERLAND GEBOREN); the native reference sample skips the migration, language, integration and Islam blocks (.c). The time-use diary (block X) was administered by the interviewer at the end of the interview, for 'yesterday', in 72 quarter-hour slots from 06:00 to 24:00 with a 43-code activity card (tim_slot01-72, tim_act01-43; day of the week in tim_weekday, diary weights tim_wgt and tim_wgt_corr); it was skipped when the interview had run long and completed by 74% of respondents (Turks 71%, Moroccans 65%, natives 87%).
- *languages*: Written Turkish and Moroccan-Arabic translations (two independent translators, reconciled with SCP) supported interviews in Dutch; respondents with language problems were re-approached by 17 Turkish and Moroccan interviewers (128 interviews).
- *release*: The DANS file holds the questionnaire variables, SCP constructs (societal position, earner type, labour-force status) and weights (svy_wgt, svy_wgt_grp, svy_wgt_raise); no registry linkage. The questionnaire itself is appendix 1a of the deposited fieldwork report.

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>SIM 2006 - Face-to-face (CAPI)</summary>

- *mode*: Face-to-face CAPI interviews (Veldkamp/TNS NIPO, with ERC interviewers for Turkish and Moroccan respondents) with persons aged 15+ sampled by CBS from the GBA nationwide (at least 10 addresses per municipality); a paper version existed for interviewers without a laptop. Fieldwork March 2006 - January 2007; corrected response 53% (Moroccans 50%, Turks 60%, Antilleans 54%, Surinamese 46%, natives 55%); 5,250 interviews. Part of the sample received two postage stamps with the invitation letter as an incentive experiment.
- *order*: Fixed block order A-P; no rotation or randomisation reported.
- *routing*: Only the sampled person answered (the partner could be present). Items on Islam were routed to Muslims by the script; a respondent counted as native Dutch when both parents were born in the Netherlands. Answer cards were collected in a card booklet and read out literally. The deposited questionnaire is the CAPI script printout, which carries no variable names: items are linked to the data through the question number in the data labels and the option order of multiple-response questions.
- *languages*: Turkish and Moroccan-Arabic written translations (one translator, independent check); first-generation Turks and Moroccans who arrived at 15 or older were assigned to co-ethnic interviewers where possible, with gender matching.

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>SING 2009 - Face-to-face (CAPI)</summary>

- *mode*: Face-to-face CAPI interviews (Veldkamp/TNS NIPO; 243 native and 60 bilingual interviewers) with persons aged 15+ sampled by CBS from the GBA in two stages (municipalities, then persons): Afghans, Iraqis, Iranians, Somalis, Chinese, Poles and a native Dutch reference sample. The Polish sample was redesigned after a pilot to short-stay Poles (less than five years registered), 532 of whom completed a Polish self-completion version on the interviewer's laptop. Fieldwork February 2009 - February 2010; corrected response 43% (Iranians 44%, Iraqis 48%, Afghans 49%, Somalis 38%, Chinese 38%, Poles 42%, natives 46%); 6,911 interviews.
- *order*: Fixed block order A-U; no rotation reported. One item, Q2630 (leisure-time contact with native Dutch, soc_leis_nl), was asked to a random half of the respondents with a migration background (CAPI script field exp2431 = 1); the deposit documents neither the split nor an indicator for it, so the half is visible only as .c on that variable (3,017 of 5,952 asked; the follow-up Q2640 went to both halves).
- *routing*: Natives skip the migration-history and civic-integration blocks (shorter questionnaire, 40 instead of 56 minutes); Chinese respondents could skip the religion items. Respondents aged 15-17 were asked to call in a parent for the household-income questions (hh_inc_band_par). The deposited questionnaire is the CAPI script printout without variable names (linked via the question numbers in the data labels).
- *languages*: Questionnaire, letter and folder translated into Farsi, Arabic, Dari, Somali, Chinese and Polish (DaVinci Vertalingen, checked by co-ethnic interviewers) and programmed in CAPI; short-stay respondents were approached by bilingual interviewers where possible.
- *release*: Partial release: the DANS file contains only the questions listed in the deposit's READ ME (the rest is available through CBS Remote Access), and years and durations are coarsened into classes: age and partner's age in 3 classes (15-24, 25-44, 45+), length of stay 0-5/5-10/10-15/15+ years, year of marriage and of first arrival in decade bands, contractual hours in 4 classes, education in 4 classes. The IMPD keeps these as the SING-only `_cat` variants (e.g. dem_age_cat3, mig_dur_nl_cat4). The release is also statistically protected: in some variables real values are replaced by 'don't know' / 'not applicable' / 'other' codes (sex for 2 respondents, marital status 71, origin group 85 - the 'unknown' group -, generation 29 besides the natives, year of marriage 39, small categories of the household-position items recoded to 98), household size and the number of children are top-coded at 6, and the BMI is delivered in classes; the resulting .d / unknown values are protection, not non-response. The CBS microdata hold the unprotected values.

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>SIM 2011 - Face-to-face (CAPI) main survey (the mixed-mode experiment is not in this deposit)</summary>

- *mode*: Face-to-face CAPI interviews at home (GfK with Labyrinth co-ethnic interviewers), no proxies, with persons aged 15+ sampled by CBS from the GBA stratified in six municipality strata (Turks, Moroccans, Surinamese, Antilleans/Arubans, native Dutch). Fieldwork from November 2010 for about five months; corrected response Turks 54%, Moroccans 50%, Surinamese 43%, Antilleans 48%, natives 55%; 4,125 interviews. A parallel mixed-mode experiment (web, then telephone, then face-to-face; 2,698 respondents, shortened web questionnaire) is NOT in the DANS deposit: all records have onderzoek = main study and methode = CAPI (svy_fw_phase records the two fieldwork phases, the second being a re-approach of non-respondents by another interviewer).
- *order*: Fixed block order A-U; no rotation or randomisation reported. Ranking question Q1073 (fam_val_rank) asks for a 1-5 order of child-rearing values.
- *routing*: Group routing as in SIM 2006 (natives .c for migrant-only items; Islam items to Muslims). Partner items Q53-70, 225, 230 are proxy answers by the respondent. Respondents aged 15-17 were asked to call in a parent for the household questions (suffix _par). The deposit is statistically protected (mu-Argus on sex x 5-year age class) and version 3 removed the open-answer variables; the questionnaire is the hardcopy of the CAPI script (appendix g), which prints variable names next to the questions.
- *languages*: Turkish and Moroccan-Arabic translations (SIM 2006 versions reused, new items double-translated); Berber (138 interviews), Papiamento (121) and Surinamese languages (11) used orally as fallback (svy_lang_hh, svy_lang_oth). All Turkish and Moroccan respondents were interviewed by co-ethnic interviewers, Surinamese and Antilleans half by native interviewers.

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>SIM 2015 - Sequential mixed mode: CAWI, then CAPI</summary>

- *mode*: Sequential mixed mode: web (CAWI) invitation first, face-to-face (CAPI) follow-up of non-respondents by bilingual interviewers (TNS NIPO and Labyrinth); CAWI and CAPI questionnaires are parallel (questionnaire_items.csv holds both; wording.csv references the CAWI version with the CAPI question id in capi_qid).
- *order*: Fixed block order with randomised item order within batteries: Q801-Q815 and Q813-Q817 (opinion statements), Q895-Q89801 (opinions on NL), Q770 contact with groups and Q859-Q865 feeling thermometers (groups presented in random order, own group always last; Jews never first).
- *routing*: Many items asked only to respondents with a migration background (ASK ONLY IF not Q9001=7); the native reference sample gets mirrored wording ('allochtone' instead of 'autochtone' contacts).
- *languages*: Questionnaire available in Dutch, Turkish, Moroccan Arabic, Polish and Somali (CAWI language choice; language variable not in the public file).

</details>


<details class='more'><summary>SIM 2020 - CAWI (90%) with CAPI follow-up for five groups (10%, incl. 15 video interviews)</summary>

- *mode*: CAWI (90%) with CAPI follow-up only for the Caribbean, Moroccan, Somali, Surinamese and Turkish groups (10%) because of covid; 15 CAPI interviews by video call (WhatsApp). Fieldwork 11 March 2020 - 17 January 2021 with CAPI suspended during lockdowns.
- *split_half*: Respondents randomly assigned within origin group to A or B (svy_split). Only A: political participation (POL_4, HERK_3), institutional trust (VERTWORG), belonging (CONTACTERBIJ, ORGANBIJ), media interest and positioning (NIEUWS_3, FREQNIEU, FREQAANT, POS_4). Only B: opinion statements STELL_8_12 and STELL_1_7_5, religion items BIJBKOR and KORZELFINT, mental health items MENTALGEZ_4_4, 8_3, 8_4, BEZOEKMOG, HUISARTS, PIJN, situational discrimination DISCZELF2, Zwarte Piet items.
- *order*: Fixed block order with randomised item order within batteries: Q801-Q804, Q813-Q817, Q895-Q89801, Q965-Q967.
- *versions*: Six script versions (svy_qversion); version differences are not documented in the fieldwork report. Early CAWI interviews ran on versions 1-3.
- *languages*: Dutch, Turkish, Moroccan Arabic, Polish, Somali, Farsi (svy_lang_q); a Farsi error in two items is flagged in the source (code -1).
- *wording*: Group terms updated: 'allochtoon' -> 'persoon met een migratieachtergrond' in most items; 'autochtone Nederlanders' retained in contact items. Text fills per group (<HERKGRP>, <LVH>).

</details>

## 5. Variable descriptions {#descriptions}

---

### `id_person` {#id_person}
**Unique person identifier (svy_key*1e11 + source person/record number; household samples: id_hh*100 + member number)**
- Theme: Identifiers (`id`) · Scope: person · Type: id
- Universe: All household members (roster)
- Derived: `id_person` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: Constructed; unique across surveys and unchanged when a survey is added (svy_key = fieldwork year, never renumbered; surveys.csv). Stored as double.
- Subject: identifier · Reported by: constructed (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020)
- Availability: derived: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020
- Comparability: **administrative** (auto) — identifier or survey-administration variable

Identifier (no descriptives: the values are labels, not quantities):

| survey | n non-missing | n distinct | unique within survey |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPVA2002 | 13504 | 13504 | yes |
| SPVN2003 | 9119 | 9119 | yes |
| LAS2004 | 4096 | 4096 | yes |
| SIM2006 | 5250 | 5250 | yes |
| SING2009 | 6911 | 6911 | yes |
| SIM2011 | 4125 | 4125 | yes |
| SIM2015 | 6829 | 6829 | yes |
| SIM2020 | 5323 | 5323 | yes |

---

### `id_prtnr` {#id_prtnr}
**Identifier (id_person) of the co-resident partner's own record in the household roster**
- Theme: Identifiers (`id`) · Scope: person · Type: id
- Universe: Heads of household and their partners in the household samples (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003); person samples .e
- Derived: `id_prtnr` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: Link of the relationship layer: the other head/partner member (dem_poshh 0 or 1) of the same household when exactly one exists. .c = no co-resident partner record; .d = not identifiable (other household members; no roster in the DANS files has more than two head/partner records). Stored as double.
- Subject: identifier · Reported by: constructed from the roster (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)
- Availability: derived from the roster link: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003 · not collected: LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020
- Comparability: **administrative** (auto) — identifier or survey-administration variable

Identifier (no descriptives: the values are labels, not quantities):

| survey | n non-missing | n distinct | unique within survey |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPVA2002 | 5098 | 5098 | yes |
| SPVN2003 | 2454 | 2454 | yes |
| LAS2004 | 0 | 0 | - |
| SIM2006 | 0 | 0 | - |
| SING2009 | 0 | 0 | - |
| SIM2011 | 0 | 0 | - |
| SIM2015 | 0 | 0 | - |
| SIM2020 | 0 | 0 | - |

| .d | No information | 6756 | 4345 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| .e | Not collected (survey/questionnaire) | 0 | 0 | 4096 | 5250 | 6911 | 4125 | 6829 | 5323 |

### `id_hh_src` {#id_hh_src}

- Theme: Identifiers (`id`) · Scope: person · Type: id
- Universe: All household members (roster) (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)
- Sources (file level): SPVA 2002 `HHNUMMER` (ro,pp,hh); SPVN 2003 `HHNUMMER` (ro,pp,hh)
- Notes: Source household number; not unique across surveys - use id_hh.
- Subject: identifier · Reported by: registry / survey administration (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)
- Availability: collected: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003 · not collected: LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020

| How obtained | registry/sample data | registry/sample data |
| Information supplied by | registry / survey administration | registry / survey administration |
| Person / entity described | identifier | identifier |
| Question / statement shown or read to respondent | Not applicable - registry / sample-frame field (see the source definition row) | Not applicable - registry / sample-frame field (see the source definition row) |
| Source definition / derivation | Registry (CBS microdata) or survey-administration field, no questionnaire item | Registry (CBS microdata) or survey-administration field, no questionnaire item |

| Eligible records / population | All household members (roster) (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003) | All household members (roster) (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003) |

### `id_mem` {#id_mem}
**Household member number within household**
- Theme: Identifiers (`id`) · Scope: person · Type: cat · Value set: `member_number`
- Universe: All household members (roster) (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)
- Sources (file level): SPVA 2002 `GEZLIDNR` (ro,pp,hh); SPVN 2003 `GEZLIDNR` (ro,pp,hh)
- Notes: 0 = head, 1-9 = children by age rank, 10 = partner, 11-18 = other members.
- Subject: identifier · Reported by: registry / survey administration (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)
- Availability: collected: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003 · not collected: LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020
- Comparability: **administrative** (auto) — identifier or survey-administration variable
- Wording and procedure: Registry/sample fields (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003): see the source definition row

|---|---|---|
| Source variable | `GEZLIDNR` (no questionnaire item (registry/administrative)) — *Gezinslidnummer* | `GEZLIDNR` (no questionnaire item (registry/administrative)) — *Gezinslidnummer* |
| How obtained | registry/sample data | registry/sample data |
| Information supplied by | registry / survey administration | registry / survey administration |
| Person / entity described | identifier | identifier |

### `svy_routing_mig` {#svy_routing_mig}
**Received the migrant-background routing of the CAPI script (person samples)**
- Theme: Survey design and interview (`svy`) · Scope: person · Type: cat · Value set: `yesno`
- Universe: Individually sampled respondents (LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020)
- Derived: `routing_mig` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: Derived: 1 when any of the gate items asked only to persons with a migration background carries an answer (lang_prob_spk, lang_prob_read, iden_scale, iden_orig5, int_crs, int_nlcrs, trn_house, med_krant_orig_cat; items that some survey asks to natives, such as ret_wish in SING 2009 or iden_nl5 in SIM 2020, are not gates), 0 otherwise. The scripts route on the sample-frame origin group, which the deposits do not deliver; dem_eth is the self-reported group (SCP construction from the respondent's and parents' countries of birth). Self-reported natives with routing 1 were sampled in a migrant group (LAS 24, SIM 2011 23, SING 3); their answers are kept. The universe check uses this flag instead of a tolerance.
- Subject: interview · Reported by: constructed (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020)
- Availability: derived: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020
- Comparability: **administrative** (auto) — identifier or survey-administration variable

- Notes: SPVA 2002: WEEG missing for 2,063 roster-only persons; weights constructed on demographic population data (see DANS documentation 2.8.3). Weights are survey-specific and not comparable across surveys.

### `dem_brthcntry` {#dem_brthcntry}
**Country of birth**
- Theme: Demography and household position (`dem`) · Scope: person · Type: cat · Value set: `country`
- Universe: All household members (roster)
- Sources (file level): SPVA 2002 `GEBLAND` (ro,pp,hh); SPVN 2003 `GEBLAND` (ro,pp,hh)
- Derived: `brthcntry_group` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: Harmonized to Landentabel (Tabel 34) codes; survey lists only distinguish the target-group countries, NL and 'other'. Observed in SPVA 2002 / SPVN 2003 only; in the person samples inferred from origin group and generation - see dem_brthcntry_src before relying on it. SIM 2015/2020: derived from dem_eth x dem_gen (CBS definition), see wording note.
- Subject: self · Reported by: constructed (LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020); respondent for the cited item; roster members not interviewed: the head of household's roster report; interviewed members: the mini questionnaire (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)
- Availability: collected: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003 · derived where the inputs exist: LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020
- Routing (harmonized variables): none printed (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)
- Comparability: **derived** (auto) — derived by rule 'brthcntry_group' in every survey where the inputs exist; see the variable note
- Wording and procedure: Respondent-facing (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003): question differs (SPVN 2003 vs SPVA 2002); introduction none printed; answer options differs (SPVN 2003 vs SPVA 2002). **Note:** SIM public files do not contain country of birth (removed by DANS/SCP). Under the CBS definition the origin group of a first-generation person is his/her own country of birth and second-generation persons are born in the Netherlands, so dem_brthcntry is derived (derive brthcntry_group): first generation -> country of the origin group (Caribbean group -> 7011 aggregate), second generation and natives -> 6030 Netherlands.

### `dem_brthcntry_src` {#dem_brthcntry_src}
**Provenance of dem_brthcntry: observed in the survey or inferred from origin group x generation**
- Theme: Demography and household position (`dem`) · Scope: person · Type: cat · Value set: `brthcntry_src`
- Universe: All household members (roster)
- Derived: `brthcntry_src` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: 1 = country of birth as collected (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003 household roster); 2 = inferred under the CBS definition in the person samples (LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020), whose public files contain no country of birth: first generation -> the country of the origin group (Chinese 6022, Caribbean 7011 aggregate), second generation and natives -> Netherlands; 'other'/unknown origin groups of the first generation are .d. The inference is a proxy, not an observation: 22 native-origin respondents inferred as born in the Netherlands nevertheless have an arrival year (LAS 2004/05 12, SIM 2006 2, SIM 2011 7, SING 2009 1; in SIM 2006 the arrival year was asked only of those who reported a birthplace outside the Netherlands), so some of them were born abroad. Where country of birth is central to an analysis, condition on this flag (follow-up audit of v0.4.8).
- Subject: self · Reported by: constructed (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020)
- Availability: derived: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020
- Comparability: **derived** (auto) — derived by rule 'brthcntry_src' in every survey where the inputs exist; see the variable note

### `nat_cit` {#nat_cit}
**Citizenship (harmonized)**
- Theme: Nationality and legal status (`nat`) · Scope: person · Type: cat · Value set: `citizenship`
- Universe: All interviewed persons aged 12+ (main and mini questionnaire)
- Sources (file level): SPVA 2002 `NATIONAL` (pp,hh); SPVN 2003 `NATIONAL` (pp,hh); SIM 2006 `NATIONAL` (main)
- Derived: `cit_nl_orig` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: SPVA 2002: 1 origin nationality -> 3, 2 Dutch -> 1, 3 both -> 2, 4 other -> 4. SPVN 2003: 1 -> 1, 11-24 -> 2, 111-124 -> 3.
- Subject: self · Reported by: constructed (LAS 2004/05, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020); constructed by the data producer from survey or registry inputs (see source definition) (SPVN 2003); respondent (SIM 2006); respondent (main questionnaire for heads, mini questionnaire for other interviewed members) (SPVA 2002)
- Availability: collected: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, SIM 2006 · derived where the inputs exist: LAS 2004/05, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020
- Routing (harmonized variables): none printed (SPVA 2002, SIM 2006)
- Comparability: **derived** (auto) — derived by rule 'cit_nl_orig' in every survey where the inputs exist; see the variable note
- Wording and procedure: Respondent-facing (SPVA 2002, SIM 2006): question identical; introduction none printed; answer options differs (SIM 2006 vs SPVA 2002). Constructed sources (SPVN 2003): see the source definition row. Acquisition differs between surveys (respondent vs constructed): the measurements are not equivalent by wording. **Note:** SPVA/SPVN: one question on nationality. SIM: two yes/no questions (Dutch nationality; origin-country nationality) combined (derive cit_nl_orig): 1 Dutch only, 2 dual, 3 origin only, 4 neither/other.

### `rel_den_det` {#rel_den_det}
**Religious denomination, detailed (harmonized list)**
- Theme: Religion (`rel`) · Scope: person · Type: cat · Value set: `religion_det`
- Universe: All interviewed persons aged 12+ (main and mini questionnaire)
- Sources (file level): SPVA 2002 `RELIGIE0` (pp,hh); SPVN 2003 `RELIGIE0` (hh); LAS 2004/05 `RELIGIE` (main); SIM 2006 `RELIGIE` (main); SING 2009 `RELIGIE` (main); SIM 2011 `RELIGIE` (main); SIM 2015 `CATreligie` (main); SIM 2020 `religie_kl` (main)
- Derived: `rel_merge20` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: SIM 2015: CATreligie 0 is .d in the value map and becomes 0 'No religion' through the rule rel_none only for respondents who say they belong to no religion (rel_any 0); the 40 respondents with a religion but no denomination (gelooft 1, blank denomination) stay .d. CATreligie 4 'Christelijk: Overig' also holds open 'other religion' answers that the SCP coded into the classes, so the DANS and CBS (restricted component) distributions of the other-religion codes differ by design. SIM 2020 (CCF classes): religie_kl 1 Shia -> 21, 2 Sunni -> 22, 3 other Islam -> 25, 4 Christian -> 38, 9 -> .d; religie2_kl 1 Islam -> 25, 2 RC -> 31, 3 Hervormd -> 32, 4 PKN -> 39, 5/6 Christian general/other -> 38, 7 Hindu -> 13, 9 -> .d. SIM: respondents without a religion (rel_any = 0) are coded 0 (derive rel_none).
- Subject: self · Reported by: respondent (LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020); respondent (main questionnaire for heads, mini questionnaire for other interviewed members) (SPVA 2002); respondent (main questionnaire: heads of household) (SPVN 2003)
- Availability: collected: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020
- Routing (harmonized variables): `rel_any` in {1} (SPVA 2002, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2011); none printed (SPVN 2003, SIM 2006, SING 2009); printed condition not translated (SIM 2015); `dem_eth` in {1,2,3,4,7,9,10,90} (SIM 2020)
- Comparability: **derived** (auto) — derived by rule 'rel_merge20' in every survey where the inputs exist; see the variable note
- Wording and procedure: Respondent-facing (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020): question differs (SPVA 2002/SPVN 2003/LAS 2004/05/SIM 2006/SING 2009/SIM 2011/SIM 2020 vs SIM 2015); introduction none printed; answer options differs (SIM 2011/SIM 2015 vs SPVA 2002 vs SIM 2006 vs LAS 2004/05 vs SPVN 2003 vs SING 2009 vs SIM 2020); interviewer instruction identical; none printed in SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SING 2009, SIM 2015, SIM 2020; routing differs (SIM 2015 vs SPVA 2002 vs LAS 2004/05 vs SIM 2020 vs SIM 2011); none printed in SPVN 2003, SIM 2006, SING 2009. **Note:** SIM 2015 delivered denomination in condensed categories; SIM 2020 in two coarsened class lists (rel_den_det from religie_kl for Turkish/Moroccan/Somali/Iranian groups and religie2_kl for the others).

- Universe: Heads of household and their co-resident partners (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003), from the partner's own record via id_prtnr: .c no co-resident partner; .d other household members, and partners listed in the roster but not interviewed where the base item needs an interview (roster demography is available for them); Respondents whose partner was born abroad (SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011); Respondents with a foreign-born partner (SIM 2015)
- Sources (file level): SIM 2006 `REDMI_P` (main); SING 2009 `REDMI_PA` (main); SIM 2011 `REDMI_P` (main); SIM 2015 `redmi_p2` (main)
- Derived: `partner_copy:mig_reason` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: SPVA 2002 / SPVN 2003: filled from the linked partner's own mig_reason (relationship layer, id_prtnr); the person samples hold the respondent's proxy report.
- Subject: partner · Reported by: respondent (SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015); taken from the linked partner's record (id_prtnr); the base field's reporter applies: respondent (main questionnaire for heads, mini questionnaire for other interviewed members) (SPVN 2003); taken from the linked partner's record (id_prtnr); the base field's reporter applies: respondent (main questionnaire: heads of household) (SPVA 2002)
- Availability: collected: SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015 · derived from the roster link: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003 · not collected: LAS 2004/05, SIM 2020
- Routing (harmonized variables): printed condition not translated (SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2015); none printed (SIM 2011)
- Comparability: **mixed provenance** (auto) — the information is obtained differently across surveys (linked partner record vs respondent): see the 'How obtained' and 'Source definition' rows
- Wording and procedure: Respondent-facing (SIM 2006, SING 2009, SIM 2011, SIM 2015): question differs (SIM 2006/SIM 2011 vs SING 2009 vs SIM 2015); introduction none printed; answer options differs (SING 2009 vs SIM 2015 vs SIM 2011 vs SIM 2006); routing differs (SIM 2015 vs SIM 2006 vs SING 2009); none printed in SIM 2011. Derived from the linked partner's record (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003): respondent report - no partner question, the base field's acquisition applies. Acquisition differs between surveys (linked partner record vs respondent): the measurements are not equivalent by wording

SPVA/SPVN: highest diploma abroad (edu_abr_hi_det/_cat), attendance not asked. Persons routed past the question (system-missing or code 9 in the source) are .c (derive kl9_route). SIM 2015 and SIM 2020 deliver the CCF classes, whose boundaries differ from the harmonized definition: SIM 2015 counts mavo as middle; SIM 2020 counts mavo as middle and havo/vwo as high. ### `edu_cur_lvl3` {#edu_cur_lvl3}
**Level of current education, 3 levels**
- Theme: Education (`edu`) · Scope: person · Type: cat · Value set: `edu3_att`
- Universe: Enrolled persons; SIM in classes as delivered, SPVA/SPVN recoded from the detailed level (edu_cur_lvl) (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, SIM 2015, SIM 2020); Enrolled respondents (LAS 2004/05)
- Sources (file level): SPVA 2002 `HUIDOPL` (pp,hh); SPVN 2003 `HUIDOPL` (pp,hh); LAS 2004/05 `HUIDOPL` (main); SIM 2015 `huidopl` (main); SIM 2020 `huidopl_kl` (main)
- Derived: `kl9_route` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: SCP levels: low = primary/vbo/mavo (vmbo), middle = mbo/havo/vwo, high = hbo/wo. SPVA 2002 bridge class (0) -> low. SIM 2020 code 9 -> .d, or .c for persons not enrolled (derive kl9_route). Persons routed past the question (system-missing or code 9 in the source) are .c (derive kl9_route). SIM 2020 delivers the CCF classes: vmbo-t counts as middle and havo/vwo as high, and primary and vmbo-b/k sit in code 9 together with other answers and refusals, so SIM 2020 has no identifiable 'low' class (.d, or .c by kl9_route); decisions.md section 14.
- Subject: self · Reported by: respondent (LAS 2004/05, SIM 2015, SIM 2020); respondent (main questionnaire for heads, mini questionnaire for other interviewed members) (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)

- Routing (harmonized variables): none printed (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003); printed condition not translated (LAS 2004/05); `edu_enr` in {1} (SIM 2015, SIM 2020)
- Comparability: **approximate match** (reviewed) — SIM 2020 follows the CCF class boundaries (vmbo-t in middle, havo/vwo in high) and has no identifiable low class (primary and vmbo-b/k in code 9); comparable with the other surveys only away from those boundaries - see the variable note
- Wording and procedure: Respondent-facing (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2015, SIM 2020): question differs (SIM 2015/SIM 2020 vs SPVN 2003 vs SPVA 2002 vs LAS 2004/05); introduction none printed; answer options differs (LAS 2004/05 vs SIM 2020 vs SIM 2015 vs SPVN 2003); none printed in SPVA 2002; interviewer instruction printed in SPVA 2002 only; routing differs (SIM 2015 vs SIM 2020 vs LAS 2004/05); none printed in SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003

**Highest education attended in the Netherlands, 3 levels**
- Theme: Education (`edu`) · Scope: person · Type: cat · Value set: `edu3`

- Sources (file level): SPVA 2002 `MAXOPLNL` (pp,hh); SPVN 2003 `MAXOPLNL` (pp,hh); LAS 2004/05 `MAXOPLNL` (main); SIM 2015 `maxoplnl` (main); SIM 2020 `maxoplnl_kl` (main)
- Derived: `kl9_route` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: SPVA/SPVN code -1 (no education at all) -> 0, code 0 (education abroad only) -> .c. SIM 2020 code 9 -> .d, or .c for persons without education in NL (derive kl9_route). Persons routed past the question (system-missing or code 9 in the source) are .c (derive kl9_route). SIM 2015 and SIM 2020 deliver the CCF classes, whose boundaries differ from the harmonized definition: SIM 2015 counts mavo as middle; SIM 2020 counts mavo as middle and havo/vwo as high. At those boundaries the cells are not comparable with the other surveys (decisions.md section 14); the restricted component re-derives the classes from the detailed levels.

- Wording and procedure: Respondent-facing (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003, LAS 2004/05, SIM 2015, SIM 2020): question differs (SPVA 2002/SPVN 2003 vs SIM 2020 vs SIM 2015 vs LAS 2004/05); contains an unresolved fill; introduction none printed; answer options differs (SIM 2020 vs SIM 2015 vs SPVN 2003 vs LAS 2004/05 vs SPVA 2002); routing differs (SIM 2015 vs SIM 2020 vs LAS 2004/05); none printed in SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003

### `dem_prtnr_gen` {#dem_prtnr_gen}
**Migrant generation of the partner (SIM 2006: based on the respondent's answers)**
- Theme: Demography and household position (`dem`) · Scope: person · Type: cat · Value set: `generation_prtnr`
- Universe: Heads of household and their co-resident partners (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003), from the partner's own record via id_prtnr: .c no co-resident partner; .d other household members, and partners listed in the roster but not interviewed where the base item needs an interview (roster demography is available for them); Respondents with a migration background who have a partner, whatever the partner's origin (LAS 2004/05); partners of native Dutch respondents are not classed (.c); Respondents with a migration background who have a partner, whatever the partner's origin (SIM 2006); partners of native Dutch respondents are not classed (.c); Respondents with a partner (SING 2009; partners of native Dutch respondents are coded by the same rule, so a native partner born in the Netherlands appears as second generation)
- Sources (file level): LAS 2004/05 `GENPART` (main); SIM 2006 `GENPART` (main); SING 2009 `GENPART` (main)
- Derived: `partner_copy:dem_gen` (see `code/R/03_derive.R` / `code/Stata/03_derive.do`)
- Notes: LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009 (GENPART, SCP construction): 1 = partner born abroad, 2 = partner born in the Netherlands, native Dutch partners included - the parents' clause of the generation definition is not applied (SIM 2006: all 629 partners coded 2 are born in the Netherlands, 418 of them of Dutch origin; SING 2009: code 2 = 1,324 against dem_prtnr_eth 90 = 1,192). Whose partners are classed differs: in LAS 2004/05 and SIM 2006 only the partners of respondents with a migration background (partners of native Dutch respondents are .c, whatever their origin); in SING 2009 the partners of native respondents too, by the same rule (of 949 native respondents, 42 partners born abroad = 1, 655 born in the Netherlands = 2). SPVA 2002 / SPVN 2003: the partner's own dem_gen through the roster link, where native members of migrant households also carry 2 (ISEO rule). The restricted component gives SIM 2006 the CBS definition (native partners 0). Established by the restricted component, 5 Nov 2026; scope corrected after the follow-up audit of v0.4.8. SPVA 2002 / SPVN 2003: filled from the linked partner's own dem_gen (relationship layer, id_prtnr); the person samples hold the respondent's proxy report.
- Subject: partner · Reported by: constructed by the data producer from survey or registry inputs (see source definition) (LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009); taken from the linked partner's record (id_prtnr); the base field's reporter applies: constructed by the data producer from survey or registry inputs (see source definition) (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003)
- Availability: collected: LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009 · derived from the roster link: SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003 · not collected: SIM 2011, SIM 2015, SIM 2020
- Comparability: **mixed provenance** (auto) — the information is obtained differently across surveys (linked partner record vs constructed): see the 'How obtained' and 'Source definition' rows
- Wording and procedure: Derived from the linked partner's record (SPVA 2002, SPVN 2003): derived/coded - no partner question, the base field's acquisition applies. Constructed sources (LAS 2004/05, SIM 2006, SING 2009): see the source definition row.
